name: Motion
tagline: AI calendar and task scheduler that auto-plans your workday

pricing.basis: annual billing, per user per month
pricing.notes: Official pricing URL checked; public 2026 references list Individual at $34/month monthly and lower annual pricing.

tiers.name: Pro AI
tiers.limits: 7,500 AI credits/seat/month; unlimited storage; AI chat, projects, tasks, calendar, meetings, docs, wiki, and notes.
tiers.notes: Annual/default rate; monthly billing exists but its exact toggled amount was not exposed.

tiers.name: Business AI
tiers.limits: 15,000 AI credits/seat/month; capacity planning, dashboards, Gantt, time tracking, permissions, and priority support.
tiers.notes: Annual/default rate; monthly billing exists but its exact toggled amount was not exposed.

pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (-33% advertised); exact monthly dollar amounts were not exposed; free trial
pricing.hiddenCosts: AI overages cost $0.25 per 100 credits on Pro AI and $0.19 per 100 credits on Business AI.

verdictSummary: You can build an auto-scheduler for your own tasks, but robust calendar conflict handling, integrations, and productized rescheduling take real engineering.
coreLoopDIY: Create tasks with duration/deadline/priority, read calendar availability, solve a schedule, and write time blocks back.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because the calendar stays organized without manual drag-and-drop.

alternatives.name: FlowSavvy Free
alternatives.desc: It auto-plans unlimited tasks for the next two weeks; priorities and dependencies are how the paid plan gets you.

facts.install: Create a hosted account in the web app or install the iOS or Android app
facts.engines: A deterministic scheduling algorithm; FlowSavvy explicitly says it does not use machine learning to build schedules
facts.dataFormat: Tasks, events, and settings live in FlowSavvy's cloud database and synchronize with connected Google, Outlook, or iCloud calendars; the service currently provides no general calendar import or export
facts.gapVsPaid: FlowSavvy can auto-place personal tasks but lacks Motion’s team project management, workload coordination, and free priority and dependency controls.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires an internet connection; calendar synchronization requires OAuth or app-specific credentials

alternatives.name: Reclaim Lite
alternatives.desc: The free solo plan moves focus, habits, breaks and meetings around; the planning horizon is one week.

alternatives.name: Trevor AI Free
alternatives.desc: One calendar gets task-to-time-block planning and some AI suggestions; multiple calendars and deeper automation cost extra.

facts.install: Create a hosted web account and connect one supported calendar; the web app can be installed to a home screen
facts.engines: A private per-user deep-learning scheduling model; some language features use OpenAI, according to Trevor's documentation
facts.dataFormat: Tasks, calendar events, and scheduling state are processed and stored in Trevor's hosted infrastructure, with connected calendar data synchronized through provider APIs
facts.gapVsPaid: Trevor’s free one-calendar planner does not include Motion’s project management, team collaboration, workload planning, or broader automation.
facts.setupBlocker: No native desktop or mobile app; calendar integrations require OAuth, and the free tier is limited to one calendar account

rejectedAlternatives.name: Morgen
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A polished recommendation with no permanent free plan, only a 14-day trial.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Structured Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The free timeline looks right, but calendar import and automatic replanning are paid.

notes: A good 'kinda' because the core algorithm is doable but the product promise is ongoing automation.
prompt:
Build me a personal task auto-scheduler to replace Motion. Requirements:

- Node + better-sqlite3 + googleapis. Tasks in SQLite: title, duration estimate,
  deadline, priority, done. A small Express page on localhost:4920 to add and edit
  tasks, plus a `plan` CLI command.
- Read my Google Calendar free/busy for the next 14 days (OAuth token cached
  locally); respect working hours 09:00-18:00 and a lunch block, both set in
  config.json.
- The planner is greedy, not clever: earliest deadline first, weighted by priority,
  packing tasks into free slots in 30-minute increments and splitting anything over
  90 minutes into chunks.
- Write the plan back as calendar events with a [plan] prefix. Replanning deletes
  only [plan] events and relays them, never touching real meetings.
- Overdue or unschedulable tasks show in red on the web page instead of being
  silently dropped.
- A 07:30 node-cron run replans the day and emails me the schedule (SMTP in .env).
- Single user, local only, no accounts, no telemetry beyond the Google API calls.
- Out of scope: team scheduling, mobile apps, and meeting-invite handling. It plans
  my solo work around a calendar it treats as read-only truth.
- README: the Google Cloud console OAuth setup. Budget an hour for that alone.
